newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Brash ends appearance before FEC committee.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Brash ends appearance before FEC committee.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash completed his appearance before parliament's Finance and Expenditure Select Committee on Wednesday at 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT).
Brash avoided any specific reference to the level of easing seen in the market since his Monetary Policy Statement on Friday at which he sanctioned a 100 basis point easing in monetary conditions.
However, he made the following points --
* He agreed that financial markets consider monetary conditions to be tight and the market would try to ease as much as the bank would allow.

* Although he did not deny the possibility that the market had got it right by deeming conditions too tight, he noted that in the first four months of the year currency and debt markets held conditions tighter than the RBNZ deemed suitable, "so I don't think it follows that the market is necessarily right".
* He said financial markets appear to have understood the bank's new Monetary Conditions Index framework "very well".
* He saw the possibility that September's planned referendum on compulsory superannuation could lead to downward pressure on monetary conditions if the result was acceptance of the plan.
* He said that if there was what he called "a surprise result", the bank might look at issuing a supplementary statement.

* He added it was possible the bank could change its policy stance in its September projections, which are currently based on an expectation of no change to the status quo in September's referendum, if opinion polls in the run-up indicated a yes vote. * Asked if it was possible the RBNZ had held conditions too tight for a while, he said he did not feel inclined to say the bank had made "any serious misjudgments on monetary policy in the last 12 to 18 months".
